description: Custom Ground Station (GS) radio board for the S2S-2 CubeSat project. Built around an STM32WL55JC2, with a discrete FTDI USB-serial bridge (no onboard debugger), an external RF power-amplifier chain, a 3-way RF switch, and a dedicated external SX1278 LoRa receiver alongside the STM32WL55's own internal sub-GHz radio.

files: S2S-2_GS_Schematic1.pdf (sheet 3/4: RF Power Amplifier + RF Switch)
source.extracted_by: Visual inspection of rasterized schematic pages (text-only PDF extraction was not reliable enough for pin-level accuracy).

reference_design_compared: ST NUCLEO-WL55JC2 (MB1389, UM2592), verified against ST's official user manual / I-O assignment table

mcu.package: UFBGA73 (ball designators as printed on schematic)
mcu.core: Dual-core: Cortex-M4 (application) + Cortex-M0+ (radio), integrated sub-GHz radio

MAIN_5V0.source: USB-C VBUS -> fuse F1 (SF-1206HI200M-2, 2A) -> Schottky diode D1 (PMEG3010BEA-QF, reverse-polarity/back-feed protection) -> C1 4.7uF bulk cap
consumers: RF Power Amplifier stage (via EN_AMP_5V0-gated MOSFET load switch Q1)

MAIN_3V3.source: FT232RL (IC1) internal LDO, pin 17 '3V3OUT' -- there is NO dedicated 3.3V regulator IC on this board.
consumers: RF PA bias transistors (Q3/Q4) via EN_AMP_3V3
MAIN_3V3.caveat: FT232RL's internal 3V3OUT regulator is datasheet-rated for a small current budget (tens of mA). It is powering the entire STM32WL55 + SX1278 + TCXO + RF switch logic on this board -- worth a bench check under worst-case current (RX both radios + logic) to confirm headroom.

VDDRF1V55.source: Generated internally by the STM32WL55's own SMPS step-down converter (VLXSMPS/VDDSMPS/VSSSMPS/VFBSMPS pins, external L3 15uH inductor + C21/C22/C23), feedback pin (VFBSMPS) tied to VDDRF1V55 per ST's standard SMPS-for-radio reference circuit.
consumers: STM32WL55 internal radio (VDDRF, VDDPA, VDDRF1V55 pins)

power.difference_from_nucleo: Nucleo-WL55JC2 is powered by the onboard STLINK-V3E's own USB and its own dedicated 3.3V regulator/power-management block. This GS board has no onboard debugger and instead derives its entire 3.3V rail from the FTDI USB-UART chip's internal regulator -- a materially different (and lower-current-budget) power architecture.

hse.type: TCXO (temperature-compensated crystal oscillator), NOT a plain crystal
hse.wiring: TCXO OUT -> C7 10pF -> STM32WL55 OSC_IN pin (G9). OSC_OUT (F8) is left unconnected, as expected when using an active TCXO instead of a passive crystal. TCXO VCC fed from MAIN_3V3 through R9 220R + L1 (1400ohm@1GHz ferrite bead) + C8 10nF decoupling.
hse.same_as_nucleo: Nucleo-WL55JC2 also defaults to a TCXO (X4, 32MHz) on OSC_IN/PB0-VDD_TCXO -- ST's default config is TCXO, not the alternate X3 crystal option. This part of the design matches the Nucleo reference design.

lse_32khz.evidence: PC14-OSC32_IN (ball B6) and PC15-OSC32_OUT (ball C5) have no net labels / no crystal footprint visible in the schematic -- both pins are left floating.
lse_32khz.difference_from_nucleo: Nucleo-WL55JC2 populates a 32.768kHz LSE crystal (X2) for the RTC. This GS board omits it entirely -- no LSE, so the STM32WL55's RTC (if used in firmware) would have to run from LSI (internal ~32kHz RC, far less accurate) or not be used.

rf_chain.architecture_summary: TX: STM32WL55 internal radio (RFO_LP only) -> external 2-stage RF Power Amplifier -> RF switch (throw RF3) -> antenna. RX: the RF switch's other two throws select between (a) the STM32WL55's own internal receiver (RFI_P/RFI_N, via throw RF1) and (b) a dedicated external SX1278 LoRa receiver chip (via throw RF2) -- so the board can receive on either radio while always transmitting through the STM32WL55 + external PA.

power_amplifier.designator: U2, silkscreen/symbol name is literally just "PA" -- no manufacturer part number is present anywhere on this schematic (confirmed by close inspection, not a rendering cutoff). Likely a placeholder symbol; check the board's BOM/footprint field for the real part.
power_amplifier.input: PA_RFIN <- from STM32WL55 RFO_LP via C32/C33 (20pF) + L8 (1.6nH) + R13 (2R) matching
power_amplifier.output: RFOUT -> L9 (120nH) + microstrip taper -> L10 (5.6nH) -> ... -> RF switch throw RF3
power_amplifier.bias_gating: Two load-switch MOSFET stages (Q1/Q2, SIA975DJ-T1-GE3) gate MAIN_5V0 and MAIN_3V3 onto the PA's supply pins, each turned on by an NPN digital-transistor (Q3/Q4, DTC144EKA) driven from STM32WL55 EN_AMP_5V0 (PA12) / EN_AMP_3V3 (PA11). The PA is fully power-gated off between transmissions.
power_amplifier.difference_from_nucleo: Nucleo-WL55JC2 has NO external power amplifier -- it relies entirely on the STM32WL55's own internal PA (switchable between a ~15dBm 'LP' output and a ~22dBm 'HP' output). This GS board instead always uses the internal LP output and adds a discrete external PA stage after it, presumably for extra ground-station transmit margin, and power-gates that PA stage under firmware control -- a meaningfully different, higher-complexity TX path.

switch.topology: SP3T (single-pole triple-throw). Common port RFIN (pin6) goes to the antenna matching network (C42/L11/C43/C44) -> SMA1 connector.

throws.RF3 (pin4): PA output (TX path, from the external RF Power Amplifier)
throws.RF1 (pin5): net 'RFI_RX' -- by naming and position this appears intended to route to the STM32WL55's own RFI_P/RFI_N receive input, but the exact matching/balun network between them was not fully traceable in the four sheets provided.
throws.RF2 (pin7): net 'SX1278_RX' -> SX1278 RFI_LF pin (confirmed, matches directly on the SX1278 sheet)

control.VDD (pin1): driven from STM32WL55 FE_CTRL3 (PC3) through R18 100R -- acts as the switch's enable/supply-gate line
control.V2 (pin2): driven from STM32WL55 FE_CTRL2 (PC5) through R17 100R
control.V1 (pin3): driven from STM32WL55 FE_CTRL1 (PC4) through R16 100R

switch.difference_from_nucleo: Nucleo-WL55JC2 also uses a 3-way RF front-end switch on the same FE_CTRL1/2/3 pins (confirmed from ST's own RF block diagram in UM2592) -- so the control scheme is architecturally similar. The difference is what's behind two of the three throws: Nucleo's third throw is just the chip's own RFI_P/RFI_N; this board adds a second, independent receiver chip (SX1278) on one throw instead.

sx1278_receiver.role: Dedicated external LoRa receiver (RX-only in this design)
sx1278_receiver.rf_input: RFI_LF (pin1) <- L12 18nH (shunt match) + C54 4.7pF / C55 47pF (series) <- 'SX1278_RX' net <- RF switch throw RF2
sx1278_receiver.tx_output_unused: RFO_LF (pin28) and PA_BOOST (pin27) are both left unconnected -- confirms this chip's own transmitter is not used at all.
sx1278_receiver.power: VBAT_ANA/VBAT_DIG/VBAT_RF/VR_PA area all reference MAIN_3V3, decoupled with C47-C53.
sx1278_receiver.clock: Own dedicated 32.000MHz crystal, NX2520SA-32.000M-STD-CSW-2 (Y2), with 15pF load caps (C45/C46) on XTA/XTB (pins 5/6).

spi_interface.pullups: R19-R22, 4.7k each, pull NSS/MOSI/MISO/SCK up to MAIN_3V3.

sx1278_receiver.difference_from_nucleo: Nucleo-WL55JC2 has no second radio chip at all -- this entire subsystem (SX1278 + its crystal, SPI bus, GPIOs, matching network) is unique to the GS board.

connector.cc_config: CC1/CC2 each pulled to DGND through 5.1k (R1/R2) -- standard USB-C UFP/device identification, i.e. this board presents as a USB peripheral (like a USB-serial dongle), not a host.

usb_and_serial_bridge.esd_protection: SRV05-4.TCT (D2) across D+/D- at the connector.

bridge_ic.role: USB-to-UART bridge; also the sole source of the board's MAIN_3V3 rail (see power.MAIN_3V3).
bridge_ic.uart_to_mcu: TXD (pin1) -> STM32WL55 PA3 (RX); RXD (pin5) <- STM32WL55 PA2 (TX). 3-wire only -- RTS/CTS/DTR/DSR/DCD/RI are all left unconnected (no hardware flow control / no auto-reset-into-bootloader circuit).
bridge_ic.oscillator: Internal (OSCI/OSCO pins 27/28 unconnected) -- no external crystal fitted for the FTDI chip.
bridge_ic.status_leds: CBUS0 (pin23) -> R7 270R -> LED2 (green); CBUS1 (pin22) -> R8 270R -> LED3 (blue); LED1 (red, R5 270R) is tied to the MAIN_3V3/3V3OUT node as a simple power-good indicator.

usb_and_serial_bridge.difference_from_nucleo: Nucleo-WL55JC2 has NO discrete FTDI chip -- its onboard STLINK-V3E debug probe provides both programming/debug (SWD) AND the virtual COM port over a single USB Micro-B connector. This GS board separates those concerns: it has USB-C + FTDI for a serial console only, and (as far as the four sheets show) no onboard programmer/debugger at all -- SWDIO/SWCLK are present as MCU pins but no dedicated connector for them was identified in the provided sheets.

pins.1_and_3: Tied together, routed through diode D3 (CGRM4007-G) and R10 470R toward the 'MAIN_3V3' net -- likely a protected power feed or voltage-sense line to/from an external board.
pins.2_4_6_8_10: Confirmed unconnected (No Connect) in the schematic -- bare pin stubs with no wires, not merely cropped off-page.

access_port_connector.purpose_guess: A compact wired debug/bench-test UART port, useful for talking to the GS board (or a directly-wired satellite/OBC board) without going over the RF link. Not present in any form on the Nucleo reference design.
access_port_connector.confidence: high -- all 10 pins now accounted for

differences_from_nucleo_wl55jc2_summary: No onboard debugger/programmer (Nucleo integrates an STLINK-V3E; this board has none identified in the provided sheets -- SWDIO/PA13 and SWCLK/PA14 exist as MCU nets but no connector for them was found).
USB-to-serial is a discrete FT232RL chip on a USB-C connector, not an integrated ST-LINK VCP on USB Micro-B.
3.3V rail is generated by the FT232RL's internal ~tens-of-mA regulator instead of a dedicated board LDO -- a materially tighter power budget than Nucleo's dedicated supply.

Adds a complete external RF Power Amplifier stage (power-gated MOSFET switches + bias transistors + PA IC) after the STM32WL55's internal low-power TX output -- Nucleo transmits directly from the chip's internal PA (LP or HP) with no external amplification.

Adds a second, independent radio receiver (SX1278, with its own 32MHz crystal, SPI bus and GPIOs) on the third throw of the RF switch -- Nucleo's equivalent switch throw just returns to the STM32WL55's own RX input.
Omits the 32.768kHz LSE crystal that Nucleo populates for the RTC (PC14/PC15 both float here).
Breaks out a second UART (LPUART on PC0/PC1) to a compact 10-pin 'Access Port' connector, since PA2/PA3 (Nucleo's normal LPUART1/VCP pins) are already committed to the FTDI link.
SMA-fed antenna path goes through an external PA + 3-way switch + (optionally) SX1278, vs. Nucleo's simpler internal-PA + switch + SMA path.
things_matching_nucleo_reference_design: FE_CTRL1/FE_CTRL2/FE_CTRL3 on the exact same pins (PC4/PC5/PC3) as ST's own RF front-end control scheme -- this board's RF switch control clearly follows ST's reference design.
HSE is a 32MHz TCXO into OSC_IN, matching Nucleo's DEFAULT configuration (ST ships Nucleo-WL55JC2 with a TCXO populated, not a plain crystal, contrary to what might be assumed).
STM32WL55 internal SMPS-for-radio wiring (VLXSMPS/VDDSMPS/VSSSMPS/VFBSMPS -> VDDRF1V55) follows the same topology as ST's reference design.
open_questions_for_verification_on_bench: Exact routing/matching between the RF switch's 'RFI_RX' net (throw RF1) and the STM32WL55's RFI_P/RFI_N pins -- named consistently but the physical link wasn't fully traceable across the cropped sheet views used here.
Destination (if any) of USART1_TX/RX net labels on PB6/PB7 -- appear unterminated in the four sheets provided.
Whether any SWD/JTAG connector exists on a layer/sheet not included in this 4-sheet PDF set.

PB0-VDD_TCXO is NOT wired to the TCXO enable/supply in this schematic (TCXO is powered straight from MAIN_3V3) -- confirm this is intentional vs. ST's reference approach of switching TCXO supply from PB0 under firmware control.
